items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: He and I were friends to the end. There was a white local called 310 in New York City. He belonged to it, he and Casco Williams.

ctx.x: How did they take that? Was there any -- as long as you brought the money home.

Well, I was making more in four nights playing than my father made all week. And I helped the family that way, those mouths -- every time a kid would come, it was a baby girl. And he wanted another boy so bad.

Well, he finally got a boy but I was out of high school when he was born. I was playing with older men. Well, it so happened that -- I say, I was always with older men, older men. And I learned a lot from them because they had experiences over there in France and everything. I used to listen. I couldn't say anything, but I'd listen. I used to hear a lot of things. And it was an education to me in a way, because I knew how to conduct myself from their experiences.
